title: Private deploy egress + DNS + TLS incident scratchpad
content:
Synopsis:
Intermittent failures from customer private deployment when connecting to external services (LetsEncrypt ACME endpoints, package mirrors). Symptoms surface as TLS handshake timeouts or certificate verify failures coming from pods that route egress via VPC peer to central NAT. Behavior varies by AZ and node: some pods succeed, others fail.

Observed symptoms (high-level):
- curl to https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/ -> SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in some pods (timeout during handshake).
- apt-get update / pip install failures with CERT_VERIFY_FAILED or connection reset by peer.
- Envoy upstream connect errors in pod logs: \"upstream connect error or disconnect\" then TLS handshake errors.
- DNS sometimes resolves external hostnames to internal IP (weird: e.g. example-mirror.company-internal.local).
- traceroute from failing pod stops at peering-router IP; successful pod shows path out via NAT gateway.

Past commands tried (copied from terminals):
- kubectl exec -it busybox -- nslookup acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org
Server: 10.96.0.10
Address: 10.96.0.10#53

Non-authoritative answer:
Name: acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org
Address: 13.35.92.85

- kubectl exec -it failing-pod -- dig +trace acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org
;; global options: +cmd
.                       3600000 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
...
;; Received 172 bytes
acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org.  60 IN A 13.35.92.85
;; Query time: 2 msec
;; SERVER: 10.96.0.10#53(10.96.0.10)

- kubectl exec -it failing-pod -- curl -v --connect-timeout 8 https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
* Rebuilt URL to: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
* Trying 13.35.92.85...
* connect to 13.35.92.85 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org port 443: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 8000 milliseconds

- openssl s_client -connect 13.35.92.85:443 -servername acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org
CONNECTED(00000003)
139860350123456:error:140770FC:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:
---
(no certs)

- From a healthy node: traceroute to 13.35.92.85 shows next-hop -> NAT gateway -> internet. From failing node, trace stops at peering-router IP (10.200.0.1) and times out.

- iptables -S on node shows MASQUERADE rule present on healthy node but missing on failing node.

- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-abc123 -> route for 0.0.0.0/0 target nat-0fgh present for subnet-a but NOT for subnet-b (failing).

- tcpdump on host when curl runs (failing pod): no SYNs reaching NAT gateway; SYNs stop at peering router.

Logs (selected snippets):
- envoy (pod envoy-proxy)
[2026-03-02T14:12:03.124Z] \"GET /directory\" 503 UpstreamConnectError: connection failure
[2026-03-02T14:12:03.125Z] TLS handshake failed: timed out

- kubelet syslog: \"kubenet: unable to set SNAT for pod ...\" (repeated)

Hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
1) Route table inconsistency across subnets: failing subnets lack NAT/IGW egress; peers route to central router that lacks appropriate nat target. Evidence: missing 0.0.0.0/0 route in route-table for failing subnet.
2) VPC peering does not support transitive NAT: design where peered VPCs expect central NAT but peering route policy prevents route propagation. Some AZs configured differently (human error in infra as code).
3) DNS split-horizon misconfiguration: internal DNS search/override returning internal mirror for some hosts; pods sometimes use node-level /etc/resolv.conf pointing to corporate resolver returning private IPs that have no egress path.
4) Security groups / NACL: ephemeral port ranges blocked -> TLS handshake can't complete. Less likely since SYN doesn't leave peering-router.
5) MTU/path-MTU causing TLS failure on handshake (TCP MSS clamping missing). Would see partial packets; not observed.
6) Transparent TLS inspection by customer proxy in path presenting unexpected certs -> cert verify fails. We observed both timeouts and cert mismatch depending on pod, so proxy theory incomplete.

Immediate repro steps (what to run next):
- Identify failing subnets: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters tag:subnet-id -> map pods->nodes->subnets
- Check route tables for each subnet: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=<subnet-id> and explicitly check 0.0.0.0/0 target
- From a failing node (ssh): sudo ip route show; sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v; sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward
- Run tcpdump on host for pod source IP: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host <external-ip> or host 13.35.92.85 -w /tmp/trace-fail.pcap
- On failing node run curl with --interface to force node IP and --trace-ascii to capture handshake: curl -v --interface <node-ip> https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt
- Run openssl s_client with -prexit -state to capture where handshake drops.
- Compare /etc/resolv.conf on healthy vs failing node and kube-dns configmap for upstream nameservers.

Longer-term checks / infra corrections: 
- Ensure infra-as-code templates allocate NAT gateway route for every private subnet (and that route tables are associated correctly).
- Consider adding explicit egress IPs per subnet via EIP+NAT for consistent firewall whitelisting.
- Audit VPC peering route propagation rules; confirm not relying on transitive routing.
- Add synthetic SaaS e2e check from each AZ that validates TLS handshake and DNS resolution periodically.

Notes / gotchas discovered while debugging:
- Kubernetes CoreDNS was configured to forward to node-local caching stub that in turn used corporate resolver; some nodes had stale resolv.conf due to dhclient hooks. Restarting node-local-dns-cache fixed DNS for one node temporarily.
- A manual route table edit earlier this month introduced an incorrect association; terraform state drift suspected.
- Some pods attach to ENI on older kernel nodes where iptables config for nat table is different (iptables-nft vs legacy) causing SNAT rules to be absent.

Immediate action list (checklist):
- [ ] Confirm which subnets lack 0.0.0.0/0 -> remediate via terraform and apply (target: within 2 hours)
- [ ] Reboot or fix resolver for nodes with stale /etc/resolv.conf (short-term)
- [ ] Run tcpdump on representative failing node and upload pcap to incident ticket
- [ ] Add temporary egress allowlist to IGW for customer endpoints while we root-cause
- [ ] Coordinate with cloud networking team to verify VPC peering route settings and whether NAT/IGW reachable across peering

Notes for handoff to infra team:
- Candidate root cause: route table mismatch + missing SNAT on some nodes. Evidence: missing MASQUERADE rule, traceroute stopping at peering-router IP.
- Ask infra to check terraform routes for private subnets in account X and confirm terraform plan doesn't show drift for route-table associations.
- If infra confirms routes are good, next check is node-level ENI kernel/iptables differences (iptables-nft vs legacy) and kubelet kube-proxy mode.

Timestamps / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-03-01 09:22 - first customer report of intermittent TLS errors
- 2026-03-01 11:40 - reproduced internally on subnet-b
- 2026-03-02 14:10 - tcpdump shows SYN not leaving peering-router
- 2026-03-02 16:00 - discovered route-table no 0.0.0.0/0 for subnet-b (manual console check)
- 2026-03-03 08:15 - node-local DNS cache restarted on node-7 -> pod DNS resolution recovered temporarily

Appendix: Helpful commands (copy/paste)
- aws: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=<subnet-id> --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'
- kubectl: kubectl get pods -o wide --namespace <ns> --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node-name>
- node: sudo ip route show; sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep MASQUERADE || true
- tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -n -i any host 13.35.92.85 and port 443 -w /tmp/out.pcap

Open questions / unknowns to investigate:
- Why do some subnets have correct routes and others not — manual console change vs terraform bug?
- Is there any middlebox (customer-managed) doing TLS interception for a subset of AZs? (ask customer network team)
- Are there kernel/iptables differences introduced by recent node AMI update that removed nat table rules?

If I don't respond in Slack: escalate to infra on-call (Miguel) with note: \"Subnet <subnet-b> missing 0.0.0.0/0 route -> causes egress/TLS failures for private deployment. tcpdump attached. Please verify terraform state and route associations.\"

-- end of scratchpad --
